title: IIS Export File Compromise Confirmed

fields.to: Dr. Joanna Pruitt (HO), Wes Tran (IT), Dr. Neha Raman (Epi)
fields.subject: FW: IIS Export File Compromise Confirmed
fields.note: After full forensic analysis of MCHD-INT01, we confirm: the unauthorized script auto_cleaner.py was used to alter the IIS export file for 10-21. It inserted 412 fake MMR doses with non-existent lot numbers (MMR-2026-0044 to MMR-2026-0045). The attacker used a phishing email to compromise Jenna Fowler’s SlotWise account (MCHD-SLOT-042) and then used her credentials to bulk-cancel 640 appointments for the POD clinic in Brandt. The fake entries were designed to mimic real dose records. The attacker has not yet accessed the ClinicTrack database, but the IIS export was altered to include the fake data. We recommend immediate isolation of MCHD-INT01 and the IIS export interface to prevent further corruption.

original.subject: Suspicious Script Execution on MCHD-INT01
original.body: The script 'auto_cleaner.py' on MCHD-INT01 has been confirmed as malicious. It is actively deleting entries from the IIS export file. No digital signature. Not in approved software inventory (MCHD-FAC-SYS-2026, rev 2.0). File creation timestamp: 09:00:12. Host: MCHD-INT01. Alert level: Cyber 2. Forensic analysis in progress.

instructorNote: This is a definitive confirmation of data tampering. The Incident Commander must now declare Cyber 1 and activate EOP Level 1. The team must transition to paper mode immediately.
